text:
mike: heads-up, saw a spike of OOMs on a 8xA100 tp=2 inference job running large kv-cache loads, filing here for visibility
ana: thanks. symptoms? single-GPU or cross-node?

mike: multi-gpu on one node. logs show NCCL allocation + ephemeral tempbufs growing during generation. model fit until kv-cache warmed, then we hit OOM on comm buffers.

taylor: can you paste the allocator snapshot? curious about staging vs ephemeral arena usage.

mike: pasted below (trimmed):
```
[allocator] reserved: 16256MB, used: 14560MB
[staging_arena] sticky: 2048MB free: 128MB
[comm_pool] prealloc: 2x 512MB, active ephemeral: 1.2GB
[kv_cache] total: 6.4GB (sharded across tp=2)
```

ana: interesting — comm_pool prealloc + kv cache + tp shard working set pushes working set close to device mem. Do we know which kernel path is triggering bigger temps?

mike: from profiler: attention kernel 2 (optimized) uses less temp, but fallback path for rotary + complex past-key gather falls back to a slower kernel that allocs an extra workspace (~256MB per shard). See snippet:
```
Profiler: aten::scaled_dot_product_attention -> kernel_path=fallback_workspace, workspace=256MB
```

shay: that lines up with batching heuristics we adjusted last week. Larger effective batch lengths can cause kernel selection to choose fallback. Did the run use the new batch-slicing change?

mike: yes slice-batch=auto (new heuristic). It ended up concatenating sequences to reduce overhead which increased sequence length variance and forced fallback.

rachel: proposal: reduce comm_pool prealloc to 256MB per rank and add a high-watermark for ephemeral temp allocations so we can evict comm buffers earlier. Also adjust batch-slicing to cap seq_len before concat.

ana: +1. Also try enabling kv-cache prefix compression for this job (saves ~18% mem on our microbenchmarks).

taylor: quick test plan:
1) set COMM_POOL_PREALLOC=256MB
2) set EPHEMERAL_WATERMARK=0.7 (evict at 70% used)
3) disable auto-concat for slices > 1024 tokens
4) enable KV_PREFIX_COMPRESSION=1
We'll run the same workload with perf counters and nccl debug.

mike: started a run with those flags, building now. infra-bot: can you tag the node with perf profile?

infra-bot: perf job queued: job=perf-1765432100-1 node=node-gpu-12 collect=kv,comm,alloc profile=nvprof

shay: if that reduces headroom issues we should also consider changing kernel selection threshold: prefer kernel_path=optimized up to seq_len 1536, fallback only if memory budget allows. That prevents unnecessary workspace fallback.

rachel: note: changing kernel thresholds might slightly increase latency for some mid-length sequences (more kernels to try), but it's worth it if we avoid OOMs and cross-GPU spill. We'll add a canary config.

mike: perf results back: run with tuned flags completed without OOM and 3% higher token latency. logs:
```
result: success tokens_per_sec=1580 -> baseline 1630 (-3%)
mem_peak=15840MB -> baseline 16256MB (-2.6%)
comm_pool_peak=512MB -> 300MB
kv_cache=6.1GB (after prefix compress)
```

ana: great. comm_pool reduction + kv prefix compress did most of the work. The real win was EPHEMERAL_WATERMARK eviction preventing comm buffers from accumulating.

taylor: next steps:
- land config toggles behind feature flag (tp-comm-tune)
- add automated perf regression test to track tokens/s and mem_peak for this workload
- add a metric for fallback_workspace_count -> alerts if > 1% of calls

rachel: also add a short-term patch to allocator: make staging arena release freed sticky buffers when ephemeral demand spikes (reduce double-reserved headroom).

mike: I'll open PRs for the config + allocator tweak and include profiler traces. tagging @eng-releases for canary deploy.

shay: thanks team. if anyone sees a similar pattern on dedicated clusters ping here with node id and profiler dump. :thumbsup:
